say.en: A memory address like 1010 1111 0011 0100 is hard to read aloud. Engineers write it as AF34. That is hexadecimal. In this lesson: Describe the octal and hexadecimal systems.
Convert between binary, octal, hexadecimal and decimal.

body.en: *Octal* has base 8 with digits 0–7; since $8 = 2^3$, each octal digit stands for exactly 3 bits. Hexadecimal has base 16 with digits 0–9 and A–F (A = 10 … F = 15); since $16 = 2^4$, each hex digit stands for exactly 4 bits. They are compact ways to write binary numbers.

points.en: Hex: base 16, digits 0–9, A–F, 4 bits per digit

narration.en: Octal groups bits in threes and hexadecimal groups them in fours. Hex uses letters A to F for ten to fifteen.
narration.kn: ಅಷ್ಟಮಾನ ಬಿಟ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಮೂರರಂತೆ, ಷೋಡಶಮಾನ ನಾಲ್ಕರಂತೆ ಗುಂಪು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಷೋಡಶಮಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಹತ್ತರಿಂದ ಹದಿನೈದಕ್ಕೆ A ಯಿಂದ F ಅಕ್ಷರಗಳು.

title.en: On the board: Octal and hex by grouping

say.en: Take 1101011 in binary. For octal, group the bits in threes from the right, adding zeros on the left.
Each group of three becomes one octal digit: 1, 5, 3. So the number is 153 in octal.
For hexadecimal, group in fours: 0110 and 1011. That gives 6 and B, so the number is 6B in hex.
Check both in decimal. Each gives 107, so the conversions agree.
On the board: Octal and hex by grouping.

body.en: Binary → *octal*/hex: group bits from the binary point (3 for octal, 4 for hex) and replace each group by its digit; pad with leading zeros. Octal/hex → binary: replace each digit by its 3-bit or 4-bit group. Octal ↔ hex: go through binary. Decimal → octal/hex: repeated division by 8 or 16.

tagline.en: Positional number systems and their bases, decimal to binary for whole numbers and fractions, binary to decimal, and quick conversions between binary, octal and hexadecimal.

myth.en: When converting 45 to binary by repeated division, I read the remainders from top to bottom: 101101 happens to work, so the order does not matter.

truth.en: The first remainder is the least significant bit, so the remainders are read from the last to the first. For fractions, the first carry is the most significant bit after the point. 45 is a palindrome-like case that hides the error. Try 156: the remainders in order are 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1; read upwards they give 10011100 (correct), but read downwards they give 00111001 = 57.

say.en: The same method converts decimal to octal (divide or multiply by 8) or hexadecimal (by 16). Some fractions never end in binary: 0.1 in decimal gives 0.000110011… in binary, so we stop after the number of places asked for.

Since 8 = 2³ and 16 = 2⁴, each octal digit is exactly 3 bits and each hex digit exactly 4 bits. To convert binary to octal, group the bits in threes starting from the binary point (leftwards for the whole part, rightwards for the fraction), padding with zeros at the ends.

goal.en: Positional number systems and their bases, decimal to binary for whole numbers and fractions, binary to decimal, and quick conversions between binary, octal and hexadecimal.

narration.en: Many people think: When converting 45 to binary by repeated division, I read the remainders from top to bottom: 101101 happens to work, so the order does not matter. Actually: The first remainder is the least significant bit, so the remainders are read from the last to the first. For fractions, the first carry is the most significant bit after the point. 45 is a palindrome-like case that hides the error. Try 156: the remainders in order are 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1; read upwards they give 10011100 (correct), but read downwards they give 00111001 = 57.

problem.en: Convert (156)₁₀ to octal and to hexadecimal.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Convert (156)₁₀ to octal and to hexadecimal.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Convert 156 10 to octal and to hexadecimal.
156 divided by 8 equals 19 r 4; 19 divided by 8 equals 2 r 3; 2 divided by 8 equals 0 r 2 gives 234 8.
156 divided by 16 equals 9 r 12 C; 9 divided by 16 equals 0 r 9 gives 9C 16.
Check via binary: 10011100 equals 010 011 100 equals 234 8 and 1001 1100 equals 9C 16.
So the answer is 234 8 and 9C 16.

steps.en: Regroup in threes from the right: 010 110 111.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Convert (B7)₁₆ to octal.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Convert B7 16 to octal.
B equals 1011, 7 equals 0111, so B7 equals 10110111 2.
Regroup in threes from the right: 010 110 111.
Digits: 2 6 7.
So the answer is 267 8.

body.en: Octal has 8 = 2³, so groups of 3 bits; hex has 16 = 2⁴, so groups of 4 bits. The exponent tells you the group size.
